subject: Comparing time stratified vs. non-stratified models

messages.author: 54d4981d6bf68eaf
messages.subject: Comparing time stratified vs. non-stratified models
parts:
Dear BioGeoBEARS users,

I am running the models implemented in BioGeoBEARS with manually modified states list only for the current land-mass configuration (to stablish non-adjacent areas) and with manually modified states accounting for paleogeography (time-stratified analysis).

I was wondering if it makes sense to compare all the models based on AIC or Akaike weights to, somehow, infer the influence (or lack of influence) of physiographic changes in the diversification of a group of lizards. Any recommendation/suggestion is welcomed!

Thank you very much in advance!

All the best,
Urtzi Enriquez-Urzelai

messages.author: 115d05260b0c341a
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Comparing time stratified vs. non-stratified models
parts:
Hi,

Yes, you can use AIC, AICc etc. to compare the fit of constant-geography and changing-geography models.  All that is required is:

1. the data is the same (same ranges at the tips)

2. the state space at the tips is the same (e.g. same max_num_areas setting) (this is part of "the data" -- the ranges -- being "the same" -- the ranges are drawn from the same list of possible ranges)

However, you cannot use the Likelihood Ratio Test for this comparison, as time-stratified and non-stratified models are not nested models. But AICc is more useful anyway, as you can compare many model variants at once, whereas LRT only works on pairs of models. 

AICc doesn't give you p-values, which some reviewers want, but those reviewers just need to get educated on the numerous limitations of p-values.

Unless your dataset is huge, use AICc instead of AIC.

Cheers!
Nick
